risk_if_not_implemented: Without Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM), counterfeit, non-conforming or compromised components and services may enter the environment through the supply chain. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to R-EX-6, R-GV-2, R-GV-5, R-SC-3, R-SC-7, R-IP-5, and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products (MT-20).

compensating_control_1.name: Publishing Security, Compliance & Resilience Documentation
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to establish, maintain and disseminate policies, standards and procedures necessary for secure, compliant and resilient capabilities.
compensating_control_1.justification: Publishing Security, Compliance & Resilience Documentation (GOV-04) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) (TDA-04.2) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Administrator Documentation
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to obtain, protect and distribute administrator documentation for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that describe:
(1) Secure configuration, installation and operation of the TAAS;
(2) Effective use and maintenance of security features/functions; and
(3) Known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative (e.g., privileged) functions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Administrator Documentation (TDA-08.3) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) (TDA-04.2) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
